objective: Review the Windows test-fix commit b1dec34..252fedc on release/0.2.0/fix/windows-tests for correctness and test integrity.
scope: It fixes 3 tests that failed only on windows-latest CI (log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/b1af37dd-2976-516b-9354-81a5e7eae819/scratchpad/job-125958444273.log): agents path compared with backslashes (plugin.test.ts), execute bit read via stat on NTFS (host.test.ts, split into a real-platform test plus a POSIX test skipped on win32), and a 5000ms timeout on a large-state session-start test running about 30 CLI starts (hooks.test.ts, now 40s).
Review only the committed diff b1dec34..252fedc. Another writer may edit the working tree at the same time, so read the committed range, not the working tree.
constraints: Read-only: no edits, no version-control writes, nothing under .git/ or .holyagent/. Scratch files only under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/b1af37dd-2976-516b-9354-81a5e7eae819/scratchpad.
Do not add requirements beyond the three failures; mark anything else non-blocking.
Report in under 400 words; put long output in the scratchpad and give its path.

result:
result: No blockers. All three fixes address their Windows failures, and the changed tests pass on Linux.

changed: none (read-only review of b1dec34...252fedc)

checks:
- `/code-review b1dec34...252fedc` ran from the built-in skill and returned 5 findings. I classified each below.
- `bun test host.test.ts plugin.test.ts` -> exit 0, 67 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail. The skip is the pre-existing `skipIf(!available)` claude CLI test in plugin.test.ts, not this change.
- `bun test host.test.ts` alone -> 6 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test hooks.test.ts -t "after a resume or compaction"` -> 7 pass, 0 fail, 6.5s.
- `HEAD` is 252fedc. I ran everything on Linux only. I could not run the Windows paths, and `windows-latest` CI is the only proof for those.

blockers: none

questions: none

notes (all optional):
- **plugin.test.ts:994, `toPosix` on a hard-coded win32 path:** it only exercises `toPosix`, not the `AGENTS` constant. It is a cheap stand-in for the Windows separator, and the first assertion does check `AGENTS`. Rejected as a blocker.
- **host.test.ts:33, new default-platform test:** it overlaps the skipIf test on POSIX and the win32 test on Windows. It is the only test that uses the real platform, and it is the one that failed on CI. Keep it.
- **host.test.ts:38, comment:** it says the win32 branch is checked by "the test below and the one above". The test above takes the win32 branch only on Windows, so the wording is slightly loose. Fix it if you touch the file.
- **hooks.test.ts:1491, 40s timeout:** this is a timeout raise, not a fix for the slowness. The comment explains why, and it sits after the `finally` inside the test body, so it is easy to miss. The work is about 30 CLI starts, and the same file may carry similar timeout settings elsewhere. It hides no defect: the assertions are unchanged and I saw no test timeout in the log's other failures.
- **host.ts:88, `indexMode` on Windows returns false for untracked files:** this was added before this range and is not in the diff, so I did not review it as a change. It is a pre-existing design choice and out of scope.

evidence:
findings: No blockers. Five code-review findings were classified: four are optional notes (plugin.test.ts:994, host.test.ts:33 and :38, hooks.test.ts:1491) and the host.ts:88 finding is out of range.
checks-run: `bun test` on host.test.ts and plugin.test.ts exited 0 (67 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail). `bun test` on host.test.ts alone gave 6 pass. `bun test` on hooks.test.ts with `-t "after a resume or compaction"` gave 7 pass, 0 fail. Windows paths were not run.
Each change addresses its Windows failure without hiding a real defect: plugin.test.ts compares `toPosix(AGENTS)`, which is the same value the plugin and git use. host.test.ts reads the committed mode on Windows and reads `stat` elsewhere. hooks.test.ts only raises the timeout, and the assertions are unchanged.
No assertion is weakened, and the win32 skip covers only behavior absent on Windows and is documented: the skipIf test skips only on `process.platform === "win32"`, and its comment says NTFS has no execute bit. The explicit-win32 test and the default-platform test still run everywhere, and no assertion was removed.
The changed tests pass on Linux: the host and plugin test runs and the hooks session-start run listed under checks-run all passed, with no failures.
